title: Co-ordinate Geometry (2D)

notes.heading: 1. Straight Lines, Distance Formulas & Circles
notes.proseLatex: For two lines with slopes $m_1, m_2$, the acute angle satisfies $\tan\theta = \left|\frac{m_1 - m_2}{1 + m_1 m_2}\right|$, giving $m_1 = m_2$ for parallel and $m_1 m_2 = -1$ for perpendicular lines. The perpendicular distance from $(x_0, y_0)$ to $ax + by + c = 0$ is $\frac{|ax_0 + by_0 + c|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}$. A general circle $x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$ has centre $(-g, -f)$ and radius $\sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}$; two circles cut orthogonally when $2g_1 g_2 + 2f_1 f_2 = c_1 + c_2$.

keyFormulas.label: Point-Line Distance & Orthogonal Circles
keyFormulas.latex: $d = \frac{|ax_0 + by_0 + c|}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}},\qquad 2g_1 g_2 + 2f_1 f_2 = c_1 + c_2 \text{ (orthogonal)}$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Compute chord/tangent distances and test orthogonality of two circles.

examples.problemLatex: Find the radius of the circle $2x^2 + 2y^2 - 8x + 12y - 6 = 0$.
stepsLatex: Divide by $2$ FIRST to make coefficients of $x^2, y^2$ equal to $1$: $x^2 + y^2 - 4x + 6y - 3 = 0$.

notes.heading: 2. Parabola, Ellipse & Hyperbola Parameters
notes.proseLatex: Conics are classified by eccentricity $e$: circle ($e=0$), parabola ($e=1$), ellipse ($0<e<1$), and hyperbola ($e>1$). For parabola $y^2 = 4ax$, focus is $(a,0)$, directrix is $x = -a$, and latus rectum length is $4a$. For ellipse $\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ ($a>b$), $b^2 = a^2(1-e^2)$, foci are $(\pm ae, 0)$, and latus rectum is $\frac{2b^2}{a}$; for hyperbola $\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, $b^2 = a^2(e^2-1)$ with rectangular hyperbola having $a=b$ and $e=\sqrt{2}$.

keyFormulas.label: Eccentricity & Latus Rectum Summary
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Extract foci, directrices, eccentricity and latus rectum of standard conics.

examples.problemLatex: Find the eccentricity and foci of the ellipse $9x^2 + 25y^2 = 225$.
stepsLatex: Standard form: $\frac{x^2}{25} + \frac{y^2}{9} = 1$, so $a = 5,\; b = 3$ ($a > b$, major axis along $x$-axis).

notes.heading: 3. Tangents, Normals & T = 0 Replacement Rule
notes.proseLatex: At a point $(x_1, y_1)$ ON any second-degree curve, the tangent $T = 0$ is obtained immediately by replacing $x^2 \to xx_1$, $y^2 \to yy_1$, $2x \to (x+x_1)$, $2y \to (y+y_1)$, and $2xy \to (xy_1 + x_1 y)$. In slope form $y = mx + c$, the condition of tangency gives $c = a/m$ for $y^2 = 4ax$, $c = \pm\sqrt{a^2 m^2 + b^2}$ for $\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, and $c = \pm\sqrt{a^2 m^2 - b^2}$ for $\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$.

keyFormulas.label: Slope-Form Tangency Conditions
keyFormulas.latex: $y = mx + \frac{a}{m}\; (y^2=4ax);\quad y = mx \pm \sqrt{a^2 m^2 + b^2}\; (\text{ellipse});\quad y = mx \pm \sqrt{a^2 m^2 - b^2}\; (\text{hyperbola})$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Test whether y = mx + c touches a parabola, ellipse, or hyperbola.

wbjeebTraps: Always divide $Ax^2 + Ay^2 + \dots = 0$ by $A$ BEFORE reading $g, f, c$ for circle centre and radius.
Distance between parallel lines $ax+by+c_1=0$ and $kax+kby+c_2=0$: equalize $(a,b)$ coefficients BEFORE applying $|c_1 - c_2'|/\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$.
Check whether $a > b$ or $b > a$ in $\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$; if $b > a$, major axis is along the $y$-axis and $e = \sqrt{1 - a^2/b^2}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Straight Lines: Angle, Distance & Pair Tests
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Two lines with slopes $m_1, m_2$ meet at acute angle $\tan\theta = \left|\frac{m_1 - m_2}{1 + m_1 m_2}\right|$; $m_1 = m_2$ means parallel and $m_1 m_2 = -1$ means perpendicular. The perpendicular distance from $(x_0, y_0)$ to $ax + by + c = 0$ is $\frac{|ax_0 + by_0 + c|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}$. Micro-check: from $(2, 3)$ to $3x + 4y + 5 = 0$: $\frac{|6 + 12 + 5|}{5} = \frac{23}{5} = 4.6$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Circles: General Form, Radius & Orthogonal Cuts
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$ has centre $(-g, -f)$ and radius $\sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}$ — but only AFTER normalizing the coefficient of $x^2$ and $y^2$ to 1 (trap: divide $Ax^2 + Ay^2 + \dots = 0$ by $A$ first). Two circles cut orthogonally when $2g_1 g_2 + 2f_1 f_2 = c_1 + c_2$. Micro-check: $x^2 + y^2 - 4x + 6y - 3 = 0$: centre $(2, -3)$, $r = \sqrt{4 + 9 + 3} = 4$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Distance Between Parallel Lines: Normalize First
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: For $ax + by + c_1 = 0$ and $kax + kby + c_2 = 0$, divide the second by $k$ so both share $(a, b)$; only then apply $\frac{|c_1 - c_2'|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}$. Applying the formula to unequal coefficients is the classic slip. Micro-check: $2x + 3y + 5 = 0$ vs $4x + 6y - 9 = 0$: halve the second to $2x + 3y - 4.5 = 0$, distance $= \frac{9.5}{\sqrt{13}} \approx 2.63$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Conics by Eccentricity + the Parabola Kit
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Eccentricity classifies conics: circle $e = 0$, parabola $e = 1$, ellipse $0 < e < 1$, hyperbola $e > 1$. For $y^2 = 4ax$: focus $(a, 0)$, directrix $x = -a$, latus rectum $4a$. Micro-check: $y^2 = 12x$ gives $a = 3$: focus $(3, 0)$, LR $= 12$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Ellipse & Hyperbola Parameter Machine
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Ellipse $\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ ($a > b$): $b^2 = a^2(1-e^2)$, foci $(\pm ae, 0)$, LR $= \frac{2b^2}{a}$. If $b > a$ the major axis flips to the $y$-axis and $e = \sqrt{1 - a^2/b^2}$. Hyperbola: $b^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1)$; the rectangular hyperbola has $a = b$, $e = \sqrt{2}$. Micro-check: $\frac{x^2}{25}+\frac{y^2}{9}=1$: $e = \sqrt{1 - 9/25} = 4/5$, foci $(\pm 4, 0)$, LR $= 18/5$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Tangents: the T = 0 Rule & Slope-Form Conditions
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: At a point $(x_1, y_1)$ ON any second-degree curve, the tangent $T = 0$ follows from the replacements $x^2 \to xx_1$, $y^2 \to yy_1$, $2x \to (x+x_1)$, $2y \to (y+y_1)$, $2xy \to (xy_1 + x_1 y)$. In slope form $y = mx + c$ the tangency conditions are $c = a/m$ (parabola $y^2 = 4ax$), $c = \pm\sqrt{a^2 m^2 + b^2}$ (ellipse), $c = \pm\sqrt{a^2 m^2 - b^2}$ (hyperbola). Micro-check: tangent of slope 2 to $y^2 = 4x$: $c = \frac{1}{2}$.

memoryHooks: Slope pair tests: equal $\to$ parallel, product $-1$ $\to$ perpendicular.
Point-to-line distance: substitute, absolute value, divide by $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$.
Circle: centre flips signs of $g, f$; radius needs $g^2 + f^2 - c$.
Normalize $Ax^2 + Ay^2$ by $A$ BEFORE reading $g, f, c$.
Parallel lines: equalize $(a, b)$ first, then $|c_1 - c_2|$ over norm.
Ellipse $b^2 = a^2(1-e^2)$; hyperbola swaps the sign: $b^2 = a^2(e^2-1)$.
$b > a$: major axis on $y$, use $e = \sqrt{1 - a^2/b^2}$.
commonMistakes: Reading $g, f, c$ without dividing by the $x^2$ coefficient first.
Applying the parallel-line distance formula to unequal $(a, b)$ pairs.
Assuming the major axis is along $x$ when $b > a$.
Using $b^2 = a^2(1-e^2)$ for a hyperbola (it is $a^2(e^2-1)$).
Quoting LR $= 2a$ for a parabola (it is $4a$).
Forgetting the $\pm$ in ellipse/hyperbola slope-form tangency conditions.
Applying $T = 0$ at a point not on the curve.
Dropping the absolute value in the point-to-line distance.
Mixing up focus $(a, 0)$ with directrix $x = -a$ for $y^2 = 4ax$.
examChecklist: Compute point-to-line and parallel-line distances in one line each.
Extract circle centre/radius only after normalizing coefficients.
Test orthogonal circles with $2g_1g_2 + 2f_1f_2 = c_1 + c_2$.
Classify a conic by $e$ before quoting parameters.
Check $a$ vs $b$ before quoting foci or $e$ for an ellipse.
Use $T = 0$ replacements for tangents at a curve point.
Recall all three slope-form tangency conditions.
